title: Tier-aware region election driven by p50/p95 telemetry and path-health penalties
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a routing policy that (1) prefers nearby/low-latency POPs for production traffic, (2) respects customer tier (free/paid/dedicated) and per-route latency SLOs, and (3) gracefully falls back to compatible model variants when path quality or POP capacity degrades. Existing selectors use static weights or single-quantile thresholds and do not combine short-term percentile drift (p50 delta) with tail behavior (p95) and active network health penalties (packet loss / retransmit rate).

Proposed approach: Implement a 'tier-aware election' algorithm that computes a composite score per POP using three components: (a) short-window p50 drift relative to baseline (captures recent shifts), (b) p95 tail absolute value (captures worst-case latency exposure), and (c) network-path penalty derived from our link health signal (packet loss / RTT variance / control-plane errors). The score will be normalized and adjusted by customer tier weight and route-specific SLOs. The highest-scoring POP is preferred; lower-scoring POPs are kept in an ordered fallback list which may include model-variant candidates (e.g., quantized or smaller-capacity variants) when the primary cannot meet SLOs.

Design notes:
- Telemetry windows: 1m for p50 drift, 5m for p95 smoothing (EWMA alpha=0.2).
- Drift calculation: delta = p50_recent - p50_baseline_percentile; apply hysteresis to avoid flip-flops (require 2 consecutive windows).
- Network path penalty: score_penalty = clip(log(1 + loss_rate*100) + jitter_score, 0, 5).
- Tier multiplier: free=0.85, standard=1.0, dedicated=1.15. This biases selection toward dedicated capacity when available for critical customers.
- Fallback ordering: prefer same-POP variant (if local capacity allows smaller quantized model), then regional POPs ranked by composite score.
- Safety: an automated circuit-breaker will mark POP as degraded if composite score falls below threshold or error-rate exceeds 1% for 3m; then reroute and kick off capacity alerting.

Why different from existing work: Instead of using a single combined 'latency health index' or just p95, this ticket formalizes percentile-drift detection (p50 deltas) as a leading indicator, combines it with p95 for tail exposure, and explicitly injects network path penalties and customer-tier adjustments. It also specifies interplay with model-variant fallbacks rather than only routing to different POPs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Composite score computed in the router matches the spec for a synthetic dataset (unit tests). 2) On canary traffic (5% traffic), selection prefers higher-tier POPs for dedicated customers when scores are equal. 3) Under injected packet-loss (simulated 2% loss) the router demotes affected POPs and triggers fallback ordering including local quantized-variant when applicable. 4) No more than a 1.5x increase in mean request latency during canary rollout compared to baseline SLOs. 5) Dashboard shows p50-drift, p95, network-penalty, and final composite for each POP in real-time.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit tests + static analysis (1 day). 2) Feature flag behind 'tiered_election_v2' and dry-run mode that logs decisions without changing live routing (2 days). 3) Canary: enable for 5% of traffic in us-west region with synthetic traffic generator and real traffic shadowing (3 days). 4) Gradual ramp to 25% with monitoring alerts enabled; abort threshold: any POP error-rate >1% or tail latency >2x SLO (2 days). 5) Full rollout by region after 1 week of stable metrics. 6) Post-rollout: 2-week burn period with automated regression detection tied to retros.
metrics:
- p50-drift detection rate (alerts/day)
- p95 absolute latency per POP (ms)
- composite_score distribution per POP
- fraction of requests using fallback model variant
- customer P99 latency by tier
- routing flip rate (changes per minute)
- on-call pages attributable to routing policy (count)
